title: حِكَايَةُ الْعَاشِقِ وَالْمَعْشُوقِ
titleEn: The Lover and the Beloved, continued
part: Night 136 · The Lover and the Beloved, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 643–649 (Night 136, continuing directly from nights-135), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 136 continues the story that the vizier Dandān tells within the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, the story of the lover, the beloved and the go-between, and brings it almost to its end. As the executioner's sword is raised over Tāj al-Mulūk, an army arrives: his father, King Sulaymān Shāh, has come for his son. King Shahramān, terrified, begs the prince's pardon; the Lady Dunyā, who was about to fall on a sword, is betrothed to her lover; the two kings feast, and the marriage contract is written before witnesses. ʿAzīz, loaded with gifts, goes home to find his mother weeping and reciting verse over the empty tomb she had built for him. Tāj al-Mulūk and Dunyā are married, and the whole company sets out for Sulaymān Shāh's city, which is decorated for their arrival as the night breaks off. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ السَّادِسَةُ وَالثَّلٰثُونَ بَعْدَ الْمِائَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-sādisatu wa-al-thalāthūna baʿda al-miʾati
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the sixth and the thirty after the hundred,
sentences.i: And when it was the hundred and thirty-sixth night,
sentences.n: The print has الميلة, a misprint for الليلة, corrected here. The small alif over the lām of thalāthūn is the print's own: it spells the word without its long alif (والثلٰثون).

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّ السَّيَّافَ رَفَعَ يَدَهُ حَتَّى بَانَ شَعْرُإِبْطِهِ وَأَرَادَ أَنْ يَضْرِبَ عُنُقَهُ وَإِذَا بِزَعَقَاتٍ عَالِيَةٍ وَالنَّاسُ أَغْلَقُوا الدَّكَاكِينَ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-sayyāfa rafaʿa yadahu ḥattā bāna shaʿru ibṭihi wa-arāda an yaḍriba ʿunuqahu wa-idhā bi-zaʿaqātin ʿāliyatin wa-al-nāsu aghlaqū al-dakākīna
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that the swordsman raised his hand till the hair of his armpit showed, and wanted to strike his neck; and behold, (there came) loud shoutings, and the people had shut the shops.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that the executioner raised his arm so high that the hair of his armpit showed, and was about to strike off his head, when all at once there was a great outcry, and the people were shutting up their shops.
sentences.n: The night repeats the last words of the one before and goes on from the raised sword. The print again runs shaʿr ibṭihi together (شعرابطه). wa-idhā bi-, “and behold”: the bi- only marks what suddenly appears. zaʿaqāt, “shouts, yells”, plural of zaʿqa, a word of the spoken language. dakākīn, plural of dukkān, “shop, booth”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ لِلسَّيَّافِ لَا تَعْجَلْ ثُمَّ أَرْسَلَ مَنْ يَكْشِفُ لَهُ الْخَبَرَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-maliku li-al-sayyāfi lā taʿjal thumma arsala man yakshifu lahu al-khabara
sentences.l: So the king said to the swordsman: Do not hurry. Then he sent one who would uncover for him the news.
sentences.i: The king said to the executioner, “Not so fast!” and sent someone to find out for him what was going on.
sentences.n: man yakshifu lahu al-khabara, “someone to uncover the news for him”: kashafa al-khabar, “to find out what is happening”. The print marks the doubled yāʾ of al-sayyāf.

sentences.t: فَمَضَى الرَّسُولُ ثُمَّ عَادَ إِلَيْهِ وَقَالَ لَهُ رَأَيْتُ عَسْكَرًا كَالْبَحْرِ الْعَجَّاجِ الْمُتَلَاطِمِ بِالْأَمْوَاجِ وَخَيْلُهُمْ فِي رَكْضٍ وَقَدِ ارْتَجَّتْ لَهُمُ الْأَرْضُ وَمَا أَدْرِي خَبَرَهُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-maḍā al-rasūlu thumma ʿāda ilayhi wa-qāla lahu raʾaytu ʿaskaran ka-al-baḥri al-ʿajjāji al-mutalāṭimi bi-al-amwāji wa-khayluhum fī rakḍin wa-qadi irtajjat lahumu al-arḍu wa-mā adrī khabarahum
sentences.l: And the messenger went off, then came back to him and said to him: I saw an army like the sea, the roaring, the clashing with the waves, and their horses (are) in galloping, and the earth has shaken for them; and I do not know their news.
sentences.i: The messenger went, and came back and told him, “I have seen an army like the roaring sea when its waves crash together. Their horses are at the gallop, and the earth shakes beneath them; and who they are I do not know.”
sentences.n: al-baḥr al-ʿajjāj, “the roaring, surging sea”, a stock image for a vast army. al-mutalāṭim bi-al-amwāj, “dashing together with its waves”: bi- here is “with, by means of”. irtajja, “to quake, to tremble”; lahum, “for them, because of them”. The print marks the doubled jīm of irtajjat.

sentences.t: فَانْدَهَشَ الْمَلِكُ وَخَافَ عَلَى مُلْكِهِ أَنْ يُنْزَعَ مِنْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-indahasha al-maliku wa-khāfa ʿalā mulkihi an yunzaʿa minhu
sentences.l: And the king was dumbfounded, and feared for his kingship that it be wrested from him.
sentences.i: The king was struck with dismay, and feared that his kingdom would be wrested from him.
sentences.n: khāfa ʿalā, “to fear for”: ʿalā marks what is feared for, and an yunzaʿa, “lest it be torn away”, says what is feared. mulk, “kingship, sovereignty”, beside malik, “king”, from the same root.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ الْتَفَتَ إِلَى وَزِيرِهِ وَقَالَ لَهُ أَمَا خَرَجَ أَحَدٌ مِنْ عَسْكَرِنَا إِلَى هٰذَا الْعَسْكَرِ
sentences.tr: thumma iltafata ilā wazīrihi wa-qāla lahu a-mā kharaja aḥadun min ʿaskarinā ilā hādhā al-ʿaskari
sentences.l: Then he turned to his vizier and said to him: Has not anyone gone out from our army to this army?
sentences.i: Then he turned to his vizier and said, “Has none of our troops gone out to meet this army?”
sentences.n: a-mā, “has not …?”: the question particle a- with the negative mā. The print itself puts the fatḥa on the alif of this word (اَمَا), which keeps it from being read ammā or immā.

sentences.t: فَمَاتَمَّ كَلَامُهُ إِلَّا وَحُجَّابُهُ قَدْ دَخَلُوا عَلَيْهِ وَمَعَهُمْ رُسُلُ الْمَلِكِ الْقَادِمِ وَمِنْ جُمْلَتِهِمُ الْوَزِيرُ
sentences.tr: fa-mā tamma kalāmuhu illā wa-ḥujjābuhu qad dakhalū ʿalayhi wa-maʿahumu rusulu al-maliki al-qādimi wa-min jumlatihimu al-wazīru
sentences.l: And his speech was not complete except (that) his chamberlains had entered upon him, and with them the envoys of the king, the arriving one, and among their number the vizier.
sentences.i: He had not finished speaking when his chamberlains came in to him, bringing with them the envoys of the king who had arrived, and among them was that king's vizier.
sentences.n: The print runs fa-mā tamma together (فماتمّ), and marks the doubled mīm. mā … illā wa-, “no sooner … than”: literally “his speech was not finished except that …”. min jumlatihim, “among their number”. al-wazīr is the newcomer's vizier, as the next lines show — the vizier of Sulaymān Shāh.

sentences.t: فَابْتَدَأَ بِالسَّلَامِ فَنَهَضَ لَهُمْ قَائِمًا وَقَرَّبَهُمْ وَسَأَلَهُمْ عَنْ شَأْنِ قُدُومِهِمْ
sentences.tr: fa-ibtadaʾa bi-al-salāmi fa-nahaḍa lahum qāʾiman wa-qarrabahum wa-saʾalahum ʿan shaʾni qudūmihim
sentences.l: And he began with the greeting; and he rose for them standing, and drew them near, and asked them about the matter of their coming.
sentences.i: The vizier spoke the greeting first, and the king rose to his feet for them, made them welcome close by him, and asked them what had brought them.
sentences.n: The print has قئما, a misprint for قائما, and فابتدأء, a misprint for فابتدأ; both are corrected here. ibtadaʾa bi-, “to begin with”: bi- names what one starts with. The subject changes without warning: the vizier greets, the king rises. nahaḍa lahum qāʾiman, “rose up for them standing”, a mark of honour. qarrabahum, “brought them near”, seated them close to himself; the print marks its doubled rāʾ.

sentences.t: فَنَهَضَ الْوَزِيرُ مِنْ بَيْنِهِمْ وَتَقَدَّمَ إِلَيْهِ وَقَالَ لَهُ اعْلَمْ أَنَّ الَّذِي نَزَلَ بِأَرْضِكَ مَلِكٌ لَيْسَ كَالْمُلُوكِ الْمُتَقَدِّمِينَ وَلَا مِثْلَ السَّلَاطِينِ السَّالِفِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-nahaḍa al-wazīru min baynihim wa-taqaddama ilayhi wa-qāla lahu iʿlam anna alladhī nazala bi-arḍika malikun laysa ka-al-mulūki al-mutaqaddimīna wa-lā mithla al-salāṭīni al-sālifīna
sentences.l: And the vizier rose from among them and stepped forward to him and said to him: Know that the one who has alighted in your land is a king not like the kings, the preceding ones, nor like the sultans, the bygone ones.
sentences.i: Then the vizier rose from among them, came forward and said to him, “Know that he who has encamped in your land is a king unlike the kings who went before, and like none of the sultans of the past.
sentences.n: nazala bi-, “to alight at, to encamp in”: bi- gives the place. al-mutaqaddimīn … al-sālifīn: the rhyme pairs “those who came before” with “those who have passed away”, and the envoy's speech keeps up this rhyming prose to the end. The print marks the doubled dāl of taqaddama.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْمَلِكُ وَمَنْ هُوَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-maliku wa-man huwa
sentences.l: And the king said to him: And who is he?
sentences.i: “And who is he?” asked the king.

sentences.t: قَالَ الْوَزِيرُ هُوَ صَاحِبُ الْعَدْلِ وَالْأَمَانِ الَّذِي شَاعَتْ بِعُلُوِّ هِمَّتِهِ الرُّكْبَانُ السُّلْطَانُ سُلَيْمَانُ شَاهْ صَاحِبُ الْأَرْضِ الْخَضْرَاءِ وَالْعَمُودَيْنِ وَجِبَالِ إِصْفَهَانَ
sentences.tr: qāla al-wazīru huwa ṣāḥibu al-ʿadli wa-al-amāni alladhī shāʿat bi-ʿuluwwi himmatihi al-rukbānu al-sulṭānu sulaymānu shāh ṣāḥibu al-arḍi al-khaḍrāʾi wa-al-ʿamūdayni wa-jibāli iṣfahāna
sentences.l: The vizier said: He is the master of justice and safety, the one whom the riders spread-abroad (word) of his loftiness of aspiration: the sultan Sulaymān Shāh, lord of the Green Land and the Two Pillars and the mountains of Iṣfahān.
sentences.i: The vizier said, “He is the lord of justice and of safety, whose high resolve the caravans have carried far and wide: the Sultan Sulaymān Shāh, lord of the Green Land and the Two Pillars and the mountains of Iṣfahān.
sentences.n: Rhyming prose again: al-amān … al-rukbān … Iṣfahān. shāʿat bi-hi al-rukbān, “the riders spread it abroad”, an old phrase for fame carried by travellers: shāʿa bi-, “to make known”, the bi- marking what is spread. himma, “ambition, resolve, magnanimity”. The Green Land and the mountains of Iṣfahān are the realm given to Sulaymān Shāh where his tale begins; al-ʿamūdayn, “the two pillars” (or “the two columns”), is not explained, and may be a place name of the story.

sentences.t: وَهُوَ يُحِبُّ الْعَدْلَ وَالْإِنْصَافَ وَيَكْرَهُ الْجَوْرَ وَالِاعْتِسَافَ
sentences.tr: wa-huwa yuḥibbu al-ʿadla wa-al-inṣāfa wa-yakrahu al-jawra wa-al-iʿtisāfa
sentences.l: And he loves justice and fair-dealing, and hates oppression and high-handedness.
sentences.i: He loves justice and fair dealing, and hates tyranny and wrong.
sentences.n: Two balanced halves rhyming in -āf: inṣāf, “giving each his due”, against iʿtisāf, “acting arbitrarily, oppression” (literally “going off the road”).

sentences.t: وَيَقُولُ لَكَ إِنَّ ابْنَهُ عِنْدَكَ وَفِي مَدِينَتِكَ وَهُوَ حُشَاشَةُ قَلْبِهِ وَثَمَرَةُ فُؤَادِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-yaqūlu laka inna ibnahu ʿindaka wa-fī madīnatika wa-huwa ḥushāshatu qalbihi wa-thamaratu fuʾādihi
sentences.l: And he says to you: His son is with you and in your city, and he is the last-breath of his heart and the fruit of his inmost-heart.
sentences.i: And he sends you word that his son is with you, here in your city, and that the boy is his heart's very life and the fruit of his heart.
sentences.n: ḥushāsha, “the last remnant of life in the body”; ḥushāshat qalbihi, “the very life of his heart”. fuʾād, like qalb, is “heart”, the seat of feeling. inna after yaqūlu: what is said is quoted, so “his son” is Sulaymān Shāh's — reported speech, not his own words.

sentences.t: فَإِنْ وَجَدَهُ سَالِمًا فَهُوَ الْمَقْصُودُ وَأَنْتَ الْمَشْكُورُ الْمَحْمُودُ وَإِنْ كَانَ فُقِدَ مِنْ بِلَادِكَ أَوْ أَصَابَهُ شَيْءٌ فَأَبْشِرْ بِالدَّمَارِ وَخَرَابِ الدِّيَارِ لِأَنَّهُ يَصِيرُ بَلَدُكَ قَفْرَاءَ يَنْعَقُ فِيهِ الْغُرَابُ
sentences.tr: fa-in wajadahu sāliman fa-huwa al-maqṣūdu wa-anta al-mashkūru al-maḥmūdu wa-in kāna fuqida min bilādika aw aṣābahu shayʾun fa-abshir bi-al-damāri wa-kharābi al-diyāri li-annahu yaṣīru baladuka qafrāʾa yanʿaqu fīhi al-ghurābu
sentences.l: So if he finds him safe, then that is the thing-aimed-at, and you are the thanked one, the praised one; and if he has been lost from your lands, or something has befallen him, then take-the-tidings of destruction and the ruin of the dwellings, because your country will become a wasteland in which the raven croaks.
sentences.i: If he finds him safe and sound, well and good, and you shall have thanks and praise; but if he has gone missing in your lands, or any harm has come to him, then look for nothing but destruction and the ruin of your homes, for your country will become a waste where the raven croaks.
sentences.n: Rhyme pairs again: al-maqṣūd / al-maḥmūd, al-damār / al-diyār. fa-abshir bi-, “rejoice in the news of”, used here in bitter irony for a threat. The raven, ghurāb, is the bird of ruin and parting, and its croak over deserted dwellings is a stock image of desolation. yaṣīru baladuka qafrāʾa: balad is masculine (fīhi, “in it”), but the print gives it the feminine qafrāʾ, “empty, desolate”, a form usually said of land; read as printed.

sentences.t: وَهَا أَنَا قَدْ بَلَّغْتُكَ الرِّسَالَةَ وَالسَّلَامُ
sentences.tr: wa-hā anā qad ballaghtuka al-risālata wa-al-salāmu
sentences.l: And here I am: I have conveyed to you the message, and peace.
sentences.i: So now I have delivered my message to you, and there is an end of it.”
sentences.n: wa-al-salām, “and peace”, closes a letter or a speech: “that is all I have to say”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْمَلِكُ شَهْرَمَانُ ذٰلِكَ الْكَلَامَ مِنْ رَسُولٍ انْزَعَجَ فُؤَادُهُ وَخَافَ عَلَى مَمْلَكَتِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-maliku shahramānu dhālika al-kalāma min rasūlin inzaʿaja fuʾāduhu wa-khāfa ʿalā mamlakatihi
sentences.l: And when King Shahramān heard that speech from a messenger, his heart was disturbed, and he feared for his kingdom.
sentences.i: When King Shahramān heard these words from the envoy, his heart was troubled, and he feared for his kingdom;
sentences.n: min rasūlin, “from a messenger”, without the article, where Classical usage would say “from the messenger”. inzaʿaja, “to be alarmed, disquieted”.

sentences.t: وَزَعَقَ عَلَيٰ أَرْبَابِ دَوْلَتِهِ وَوُزَرَائِهِ وَحُجَّابِهِ وَنُوَّابِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-zaʿaqa ʿalā arbābi dawlatihi wa-wuzarāʾihi wa-ḥujjābihi wa-nuwwābihi
sentences.l: And he shouted at the lords of his state and his viziers and his chamberlains and his deputies.
sentences.i: and he shouted for the lords of his realm, his viziers, his chamberlains and his deputies.
sentences.n: The print writes ʿalā with a dotted yāʾ (علي), the edition's habit with final yāʾ; it is read ʿalā. zaʿaqa ʿalā here is “to call loudly for, to summon”. arbāb al-dawla, “the lords of the state”, the grandees of the court. nuwwāb, plural of nāʾib, “deputy, lieutenant”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا حَضَرُوا قَالَ لَهُمْ وَيْلَكُمْ انْزِلُوا وَفَتِّشُوا عَلَى ذٰلِكَ الْغُلَامِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ḥaḍarū qāla lahum waylakum inzilū wa-fattishū ʿalā dhālika al-ghulāmi
sentences.l: And when they were present he said to them: Woe to you! Go down and search for that youth!
sentences.i: When they had come, he said to them, “Woe to you! Get down there and search for that young man!”
sentences.n: waylakum, “woe to you”, an angry or urgent exclamation. inzilū, “go down”: from the palace to the place of execution. fattasha ʿalā, “to search for”, the spoken usage, where Classical says fattasha ʿan; the print marks the doubled tāʾ.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ تَحْتَ يَدِ السَّيَّافِ وَقَدْ تَغَيَّرَ مِنْ كَثْرَةِ مَا حَصَلَ لَهُ مِنَ الْفَزَعِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna taḥta yadi al-sayyāfi wa-qad taghayyara min kathrati mā ḥaṣala lahu mina al-fazaʿi
sentences.l: And he was under the hand of the swordsman, and he had changed from the muchness of what had come to him of the terror.
sentences.i: He was still under the executioner's hand, and the terror he had been through had left him a changed man.
sentences.n: The print has كترة, a misprint for كثرة, corrected here. taghayyara, “he changed”: his looks were altered, he was pale and shaken. ḥaṣala lahu, “befell him, came over him”, a common Middle Arabic verb of happening.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الرَّسُولَ لَاحَتْ مِنْهُ الْتِفَاتَةٌ فَوَجَدَ ابْنَ مَلِكِهِ عَلَى نِطْعِ الدَّمِ فَعَرَفَهُ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-rasūla lāḥat minhu iltifātatun fa-wajada ibna malikihi ʿalā niṭʿi al-dami fa-ʿarafahu
sentences.l: Then the envoy, a turning-glance appeared from him, and he found the son of his king on the leather-mat of the blood, and he recognised him.
sentences.i: Then the envoy happened to glance round, and he saw his own king's son on the executioner's leather mat, and knew him.
sentences.n: lāḥat minhu iltifātatun, “a glance showed from him”: he chanced to look aside. The niṭʿ is the leather mat spread under the condemned man to catch the blood; the prince has been lying on it since the end of the last night.

sentences.t: وَقَامَ وَرَمَى رُوحَهُ عَلَيْهِ وَكَذٰلِكَ بَقِيَّةُ الرُّسُلِ ثُمَّ تَقَدَّمُوا وَحَلُّوا وِثَاقَهُ وَقَبَّلُوا يَدَيْهِ وَرِجْلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāma wa-ramā rūḥahu ʿalayhi wa-ka-dhālika baqiyyatu al-rusuli thumma taqaddamū wa-ḥallū withāqahu wa-qabbalū yadayhi wa-rijlayhi
sentences.l: And he rose and threw his soul upon him, and likewise the rest of the envoys; then they came forward and untied his bond and kissed his two hands and his two feet.
sentences.i: He sprang up and threw himself upon him, and so did the rest of the envoys; then they went up to him, loosed his bonds, and kissed his hands and his feet.
sentences.n: ramā rūḥahu, “he threw his soul”: in the spoken language rūḥ, “soul”, serves as “self”, so this is simply “he threw himself”. The print marks the doubled lām of ḥallū.

sentences.t: فَفَتَحَ تَاجُ الْمُلُوكِ عَيْنَهُ فَعَرَفَ وَزِيرَ وَالِدِهِ وَعَرَفَ صَاحِبَهُ عَزِيزًا فَوَقَعَ مَغْشِيًّا عَلَيْهِ مِنْ شِدَّةِ فَرْحَتِهِ بِهِمَا
sentences.tr: fa-fataḥa tāju al-mulūki ʿaynahu fa-ʿarafa wazīra wālidihi wa-ʿarafa ṣāḥibahu ʿazīzan fa-waqaʿa maghshiyyan ʿalayhi min shiddati farḥatihi bihimā
sentences.l: And Tāj al-Mulūk opened his eye, and he knew the vizier of his father, and knew his companion ʿAzīz, and he fell fainted-upon from the intensity of his joy in the two of them.
sentences.i: Tāj al-Mulūk opened his eyes and knew his father's vizier, and knew his friend ʿAzīz, and he fell down in a swoon for very joy at seeing them both.
sentences.n: maghshiyyan ʿalayhi, “covered over (in mind)”, is the regular phrase for fainting: literally “one upon whom a covering has fallen”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْمَلِكَ شَهْرَمَانَ صَارَ مُتَحَيِّرًا فِي أَمْرِهِ وَخَافَ خَوْفًا شَدِيدًا لَمَّا تَحَقَّقَ أَنَّ مَجِيءَ هٰذَا الْعَسْكَرِ بِسَبَبِ هٰذَا الْغُلَامِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-malika shahramāna ṣāra mutaḥayyiran fī amrihi wa-khāfa khawfan shadīdan lammā taḥaqqaqa anna majīʾa hādhā al-ʿaskari bi-sababi hādhā al-ghulāmi
sentences.l: Then King Shahramān became perplexed in his affair, and feared a fear severe, when he made-certain that the coming of this army was because of this youth.
sentences.i: King Shahramān was now at his wits' end, and seized with terror when he understood that this army had come on account of that young man.
sentences.n: ṣāra, “he became”, with a following participle is common in this text for “he fell to, he was now”.

sentences.t: فَقَامَ وَتَمَشَّى إِلَى عِنْدِ تَاجِ الْمُلُوكِ وَقَبَّلَ رَأْسَهُ وَدَمَعَتْ عَيْنَاهُ وَقَالَ لَهُ يَا وَلَدِي لَا تُؤَاخِذْنِي وَلَا تُوَاخِذِ الْمُسِيءَ بِفِعْلِهِ فَارْحَمْ شَيْبَتِي وَلَا تُخَرِّبْ مَمْلَكَتِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāma wa-tamashshā ilā ʿindi tāji al-mulūki wa-qabbala raʾsahu wa-damaʿat ʿaynāhu wa-qāla lahu yā waladī lā tuʾākhidhnī wa-lā tuwākhidhi al-musīʾa bi-fiʿlihi fa-irḥam shaybatī wa-lā tukharrib mamlakatī
sentences.l: So he rose and walked over to by Tāj al-Mulūk, and kissed his head, and his two eyes shed tears, and he said to him: O my son, do not take me to task, and do not take the evil-doer to task for his deed; so have mercy on my grey hair and do not ruin my kingdom.
sentences.i: He got up and went over to Tāj al-Mulūk, kissed his head, and with tears in his eyes said to him, “My son, do not hold it against me; do not repay the wrongdoer for what he has done. Have pity on my grey hairs, and do not lay my kingdom waste.”
sentences.n: ilā ʿindi, “to by”, is Middle Arabic for “over to (someone)”. The print spells the same verb twice in a row two ways: tuʾākhidhnī with its hamza, then tuwākhidh without it (تواخذ), as it would be said. shaybatī, “my grey hair”, is “my old age”. The print marks the doubled rāʾ of tukharrib.

sentences.t: فَدَنَا مِنْهُ تَاجُ الْمُلُوكِ وَقَبَّلَ يَدَهُ وَقَالَ لَهُ لَابَأْسَ عَلَيْكَ وَأَنْتَ عِنْدِي بِمَنْزِلَةِ وَالِدِي وَلٰكِنِ الْحَذَرَأَنْ يُصِيبَ مَحْبُوبَتِي السَّيِّدَةَ دُنْيَا شَيْءٌ
sentences.tr: fa-danā minhu tāju al-mulūki wa-qabbala yadahu wa-qāla lahu lā baʾsa ʿalayka wa-anta ʿindī bi-manzilati wālidī wa-lākini al-ḥadhara an yuṣība maḥbūbatī al-sayyidata dunyā shayʾun
sentences.l: And Tāj al-Mulūk drew near to him and kissed his hand and said to him: No harm upon you; and you are with me in the rank of my father. But (take) caution lest something should strike my beloved, the Lady Dunyā.
sentences.i: Tāj al-Mulūk came up to him, kissed his hand, and said, “You have nothing to fear. To me you stand in the place of my father. Only take care that no harm comes to my beloved, the Lady Dunyā.”
sentences.n: The print runs two pairs of words together: lā baʾsa as لاباس, and al-ḥadhara an as الحذران; both are kept as printed. al-ḥadhara an, “the caution is that…”, i.e. “beware lest…”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَا سَيِّدِي لَاتَخَفْ عَلَيْهَا فَمَا يَحْصُلُ لَهَا إِلَّا السُّرُورُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yā sayyidī lā takhaf ʿalayhā fa-mā yaḥṣulu lahā illā al-surūru
sentences.l: And he said: O my lord, do not fear for her, for nothing will come to her but joy.
sentences.i: “My lord,” said the king, “have no fear for her: nothing will come to her but happiness.”
sentences.n: lā takhaf is run together in the print (لاتخف). The print marks the doubled lām of illā.

sentences.t: وَصَارَ الْمَلِكُ يَعْتَذِرُ إِلَيْهِ وَيُطَيِّبُ خَاطِرَ وَزِيرِ الْمَلِكِ شَاهْ سُلَيْمَانَ وَوَعَدَهُ بِالْمَالِ الْجَزِيلِ عَلَى أَنْ يُخْفِى مِنَ الْمَلِكِ مَا رَآهُ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣāra al-maliku yaʿtadhiru ilayhi wa-yuṭayyibu khāṭira wazīri al-maliki shāh sulaymāna wa-waʿadahu bi-al-māli al-jazīli ʿalā an yukhfī mina al-maliki mā raʾāhu
sentences.l: And the king fell to apologising to him and making-good the mind of the vizier of King Shāh Sulaymān, and he promised him abundant wealth on (condition) that he hide from the king what he had seen.
sentences.i: Then the king fell to making his excuses to him, and set about soothing King Sulaymān Shāh's vizier, promising him great riches if he would keep from his master what he had seen.
sentences.n: ṭayyaba khāṭirahu, “to make someone's mind good”: to soothe, to put at ease. The print writes yukhfī with final ى (يخفى), as it often does for ي. “The king” he is to keep it from is the prince's father. Here the king's name stands as Shāh Sulaymān; elsewhere it is Sulaymān Shāh. The print uses both orders.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْمَلِكَ شَهْرَمَانَ أَمَرَ كُبَرَاءَ دَوْلَتِهِ أَنْ يَأْخُذُوا تَاجَ الْمُلُوكِ وَيَمْضُوا بِهِ إِلَى الْحَمَّامِ وَيُلْبِسُوهُ بَدْلَةً مِنْ خِيَارِ مَلْبُوسِهِ وَيَأْتُوا بِهِ سُرْعَةً
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-malika shahramāna amara kubarāʾa dawlatihi an yaʾkhudhū tāja al-mulūki wa-yamḍū bihi ilā al-ḥammāmi wa-yulbisūhu badlatan min khiyāri malbūsihi wa-yaʾtū bihi surʿatan
sentences.l: Then King Shahramān commanded the great-ones of his state to take Tāj al-Mulūk and go with him to the bath, and to clothe him in a suit from the choice of his wearing, and to bring him quickly.
sentences.i: Then King Shahramān ordered the great lords of his court to take Tāj al-Mulūk to the bath, dress him in a suit of the best of the king's own clothes, and bring him back with all speed.
sentences.n: dawla, “state, dynasty”, here the court: kubarāʾ dawlatihi are his grandees. badla, “a suit of clothes”, is a later word. surʿatan, “speedily”, stands alone as an adverb, where Classical would say bi-surʿatin.

sentences.t: فَفَعَلُوا ذٰلِكَ وَأَدْخَلُوهُ الْحَمَّامَ وَأَلْبَسُوهُ الْبَدْلَةَ الَّتِي أَفْرَدَهَا لَهُ الْمَلِكُ شَهْرَمَانُ ثُمَّ أَتَوابِهِ إِلَى الْمَجْلِسِ
sentences.tr: fa-faʿalū dhālika wa-adkhalūhu al-ḥammāma wa-albasūhu al-badlata allatī afradahā lahu al-maliku shahramānu thumma ataw bihi ilā al-majlisi
sentences.l: And they did that, and made him enter the bath, and clothed him in the suit which King Shahramān had set apart for him; then they came with him to the audience-hall.
sentences.i: This they did: they took him into the bath and dressed him in the suit King Shahramān had set aside for him, and then brought him to the hall of audience.
sentences.n: ataw bihi, “they came with him”, i.e. “brought him”, is run together in the print (اتوابه).

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا دَخَلَ عَلَى الْمَلِكِ شَهْرَمَانَ وَقَفَ لَهُ هُوَ وَأَوْقَفَ لَهُ جَمِيعَ أَكَابِرِ دَوْلَتِهِ فِى الْخِدْمَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā dakhala ʿalā al-maliki shahramāna waqafa lahu huwa wa-awqafa lahu jamīʿa akābiri dawlatihi fī al-khidmati
sentences.l: And when he entered upon King Shahramān, he stood for him, he himself, and made stand for him all the great-ones of his state in the service.
sentences.i: When he came in before King Shahramān, the king rose to his feet for him, and made all the lords of his court stand in attendance on him.
sentences.n: waqafa lahu, “stood up for him”, is the mark of honour; fī al-khidma, “in service”, standing as attendants stand. The print writes fī with final ى (فى).

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ تَاجَ الْمُلُوكِ جَلَسَ يُحَدِّثُ وَزِيرَ وَالِدِهِ وَعَزِيزًا بِمَا وَقَعَ لَهُ
sentences.tr: thumma inna tāja al-mulūki jalasa yuḥaddithu wazīra wālidihi wa-ʿazīzan bi-mā waqaʿa lahu
sentences.l: Then Tāj al-Mulūk sat telling the vizier of his father and ʿAzīz of what had befallen him.
sentences.i: Then Tāj al-Mulūk sat down and told his father's vizier and ʿAzīz all that had happened to him.
sentences.n: The print has الملول, a misprint for الملوك, corrected here. jalasa yuḥaddithu, “he sat telling”: jalasa with a following verb often just means “he set about”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْوَزِيرُ وَعَزِيزٌ وَنَحْنُ فِي تِلْكَ الْمُدَّةِ مَضَيْنَا إِلَى وَالِدِكَ فَأَخْبَرْنَاهُ بِأَنَّكَ دَخَلْتَ سَرَايَةَ بِنْتِ الْمَلِكِ وَلَمْ تَخْرُجْ وَالْتَبَسَ عَلَيْنَا أَمْرُكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-wazīru wa-ʿazīzun wa-naḥnu fī tilka al-muddati maḍaynā ilā wālidika fa-akhbarnāhu bi-annaka dakhalta sarāyata binti al-maliki wa-lam takhruj wa-iltabasa ʿalaynā amruka
sentences.l: And the vizier and ʿAzīz said to him: And we, in that period, went to your father and told him that you had entered the palace of the king's daughter and had not come out, and your affair was obscure to us.
sentences.i: The vizier and ʿAzīz said to him, “Meanwhile we went to your father and told him that you had gone into the palace of the king's daughter and never come out, and that we did not know what had become of you.
sentences.n: qāla, singular, with two speakers after it: a verb placed before its subject stays singular. sarāya, “palace”, is the Persian and Turkish sarāy, here with a feminine ending. iltabasa ʿalaynā amruka, “your case became confused to us”: we could not tell what had happened to you.

sentences.t: فَحِينَ سَمِعَ بِذٰلِكَ جَهَّزَ الْعَسَاكِرَ ثُمَّ قَدِمْنَا هٰذِهِ الدِّيَارَ وَكَانَ فِي قُدُومِنَا غَايَةُ الْفَرَجِ لَكَ وَالسُّرُورِ لَنَا
sentences.tr: fa-ḥīna samiʿa bi-dhālika jahhaza al-ʿasākira thumma qadimnā hādhihi al-diyāra wa-kāna fī qudūminā ghāyatu al-faraji laka wa-al-surūri lanā
sentences.l: And when he heard of that he equipped the armies; then we came to these lands, and there was in our coming the utmost of relief for you and of joy for us.
sentences.i: As soon as he heard it he made his armies ready, and then we came to these lands; and our coming has proved the greatest deliverance for you, and the greatest joy for us.”
sentences.n: faraj, “relief, release from trouble”, and surūr, “joy”, are paired in a little rhyme: al-faraji laka wa-al-surūri lanā. The print marks the doubled hāʾ of jahhaza.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُمَا لَمْ يَزَلِ الْخَيْرُ يَجْرِى عَلَى أَيْدِيكُمَا أَوَّلًا وَآخِرًا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahumā lam yazali al-khayru yajrī ʿalā aydīkumā awwalan wa-ākhiran
sentences.l: And he said to the two of them: The good has not ceased running upon your two hands, first and last.
sentences.i: He said to them, “Good has always come to me at your hands, from first to last.”
sentences.n: The print has وآحرا, a misprint for وآخرا, corrected here. jarā ʿalā yaday, “to run upon someone's hands”: to come about through someone. The print marks the doubled wāw of awwalan.

sentences.t: هٰذَا وَالْمَلِكُ شَهْرَمَانُ دَخَلَ عَلَى بِنْتِهِ السِّتِّ دُنْيَا فَوَجَدَهَا تُوَلْوِلُ وَتَبْكِي عَلَيٰ تَاجِ الْمُلُوكِ
sentences.tr: hādhā wa-al-maliku shahramānu dakhala ʿalā bintihi al-sitti dunyā fa-wajadahā tuwalwilu wa-tabkī ʿalā tāji al-mulūki
sentences.l: This (much); and King Shahramān went in to his daughter, the Lady Dunyā, and found her wailing and weeping over Tāj al-Mulūk.
sentences.i: Meanwhile King Shahramān went in to his daughter, the Lady Dunyā, and found her shrieking and weeping for Tāj al-Mulūk.
sentences.n: hādhā, “this”, standing alone, closes one strand of the story and turns to another: “So much for that; meanwhile…”. al-sitt, “the lady”, is the everyday word, alongside the more formal al-sayyida. walwala, “to wail, to keen”, is the women's cry of mourning; the print points tuwalwilu itself. ʿalā is printed with ي (علي), as the print often writes final ى and ي interchangeably.

sentences.t: وَأَخَذَتْ سَيْفًا وَرَكَزَتْ قَبْضَتَهُ فِى الْأَرْضِ وَجَعَلَتْ ذُبَابَتَهُ عَلَى رَأْسِ قَلْبِهَا بَيْنَ نَهْدَيْهَا وَانْحَنَتْ عَلَى السَّيْفِ وَوَقَفَتْ تَقُولُ لَابُدَّأَنْ أَقْتُلَ نَفْسِي وَلَا أَعِيشُ بَعْدَ حَبِيبِي
sentences.tr: wa-akhadhat sayfan wa-rakazat qabḍatahu fī al-arḍi wa-jaʿalat dhubābatahu ʿalā raʾsi qalbihā bayna nahdayhā wa-inḥanat ʿalā al-sayfi wa-waqafat taqūlu lā budda an aqtula nafsī wa-lā aʿīshu baʿda ḥabībī
sentences.l: And she had taken a sword and planted its hilt in the ground and put its point on the head of her heart between her two breasts, and bent over the sword, and stood saying: There is no escape from that I kill myself, and I will not live after my beloved.
sentences.i: She had taken a sword, planted its hilt in the ground and set its point against her heart between her breasts, and she was bending over the blade and saying, “I must kill myself; I will not live on after my beloved.”
sentences.n: dhubāba, “the fly (of the sword)”, is its point. raʾs qalbihā, “the head of her heart”: the spot just over the heart. lā budda an, “there is no escape from…”, i.e. “I must”, is run together in the print (لابدان).

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا دَخَلَ عَلَيْهَا أَبُوهَا وَرَآهَا فِي هٰذِهِ الْحَالَةِ صَاحَ عَلَيْهَا وَقَالَ لَهَا يَا سَيِّدَةَ بَنَاتِ الْمُلُوكِ لَا تَفْعَلِى وَارْحَمِي أَبَاكِ وَأَهْلَ بَلْدَتِكِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā dakhala ʿalayhā abūhā wa-raʾāhā fī hādhihi al-ḥālati ṣāḥa ʿalayhā wa-qāla lahā yā sayyidata banāti al-mulūki lā tafʿalī wa-irḥamī abāki wa-ahla baldatiki
sentences.l: And when her father came in to her and saw her in this state, he cried out at her and said to her: O lady of the daughters of the kings, do not do (it), and have mercy on your father and the people of your city.
sentences.i: When her father came in and saw her like this, he cried out to her, “Princess of all kings' daughters, do not do it! Have pity on your father and on the people of your city.”
sentences.n: The print writes tafʿalī with final ى (تفعلى). He fears what Tāj al-Mulūk's father will do to the city if the prince's beloved dies.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ تَقَدَّمَ إِلَيْهَا وَقَالَ لَهَا أُحَاشِيكِ أَنْ يُصِيبَ وَالِدَكِ بِسَبَبِكِ سُوءٌ
sentences.tr: thumma taqaddama ilayhā wa-qāla lahā uḥāshīki an yuṣība wālidaki bi-sababiki sūʾun
sentences.l: Then he came forward to her and said to her: I hold you exempt from (it) that harm should strike your father because of you.
sentences.i: Then he went up to her and said, “Heaven forbid that harm should come to your father through you!”
sentences.n: uḥāshīki, “I set you apart from…”: a polite formula, “far be it from you to…”; here it pleads with her not to bring ruin on him.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَعْلَمَهَا بِالْقِصَّةِ أَنَّ مَحْبُوبَهَا ابْنُ الْمَلِكِ شَاهْ سُلَيْمَانَ يُرِيدُ زَوَاجَهَا وَقَالَ لَهَا إِنَّ أَمْرَ الْخِطْبَةِ وَالزَّوَاجِ تَعَلَّقَ بِرَأْيِكِ
sentences.tr: thumma aʿlamahā bi-al-qiṣṣati anna maḥbūbahā ibnu al-maliki shāh sulaymāna yurīdu zawājahā wa-qāla lahā inna amra al-khiṭbati wa-al-zawāji taʿallaqa bi-raʾyiki
sentences.l: Then he informed her of the story: that her beloved (is) the son of King Shāh Sulaymān (and) wants marriage-with-her; and he said to her: The matter of the betrothal and the marriage has hung upon your opinion.
sentences.i: Then he told her the whole story: that her beloved was the son of King Sulaymān Shāh, and wished to marry her. “The question of the betrothal and the marriage,” he said, “rests with you.”
sentences.n: ibnu al-maliki is pointed as the predicate (“her beloved is the son of the king”), not in apposition. taʿallaqa bi-, “to hang on, to depend on”.

sentences.t: فَتَبَسَّمَتْ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ أَنَا مَا قُلْتُ لَكَ إِنَّهُ ابْنُ سُلْطَانٍ وَاللّٰهِ لَابُدَّأَنْ أُخَلِّيهِ حَتَّى يَصْلُبَكَ عَلَى خَشَبَهٍ تُسَاوِي دِرْهَمَيْنِ
sentences.tr: fa-tabassamat wa-qālat lahu anā mā qultu laka innahu ibnu sulṭānin wa-allāhi lā budda an ukhallīhi ḥattā yaṣlubaka ʿalā khashabatin tusāwī dirhamayni
sentences.l: And she smiled and said to him: Did I not say to you that he is the son of a sultan? By God, there is no escape from that I let him crucify you on a plank worth two dirhams.
sentences.i: She smiled and said, “Didn't I tell you he was a sultan's son? By God, I have a mind to let him nail you up on a two-penny plank!”
sentences.n: anā mā qultu laka, “I, did I not tell you?”: an “I told you so” in the spoken idiom, the question carried by the tone alone. khallā, “to leave, to let”, is everyday Arabic. khashaba, “a piece of wood”, is printed with ه for ة (خشبه). She is teasing, not threatening: she says it smiling.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا أَبُوهَا يَا بِنْتِي ارْحَمِينِي يَرْحَمْكِ اللّٰهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā abūhā yā bintī irḥamīnī yarḥamki allāhu
sentences.l: And her father said to her: O my daughter, have mercy on me, may God have mercy on you.
sentences.i: Her father said, “Daughter, have pity on me, and God will have pity on you.”
sentences.n: yarḥamki, jussive after the imperative: “have mercy, (and) God will have mercy on you”, said also as a wish.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ هَيَّا بِالْعَجَلِ رُحْ وَائْتِنِي بِهِ سُرْعَةً بِلَا مَهَلٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu hayyā bi-al-ʿajali ruḥ wa-iʾtinī bihi surʿatan bi-lā mahalin
sentences.l: And she said to him: Come, in haste! Go, and bring him to me quickly, without delay.
sentences.i: “Quick, then!” she said. “Go and fetch him to me at once, without delay.”
sentences.n: hayyā, “come on!”, and ruḥ, “go!” (from rāḥa), are words of the spoken language; the print points ruḥ itself. A rhyme runs through her words: bi-al-ʿajali … bi-lā mahalin.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا عَلَى الرَّأْسِ وَالْعَيْنِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā ʿalā al-raʾsi wa-al-ʿayni
sentences.l: And he said to her: On the head and the eye.
sentences.i: “With all my heart,” he said.
sentences.n: ʿalā al-raʾsi wa-al-ʿayni, “on the head and the eye”: a gladly given “at once, as you wish”, still in everyday use.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ رَجَعَ مِنْ عِنْدِهَا عَاجِلًا وَدَخَلَ عَلَى تَاجِ الْمُلُوكِ وَسَارَّهُ بِهٰذَا الْكَلَامِ وَقَامَ هُوَ وَإِيَّاهُ وَأَتَيَا إِلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: thumma rajaʿa min ʿindihā ʿājilan wa-dakhala ʿalā tāji al-mulūki wa-sārrahu bi-hādhā al-kalāmi wa-qāma huwa wa-iyyāhu wa-atayā ilayhā
sentences.l: Then he went back from by her in haste and went in to Tāj al-Mulūk and told-him-privately this speech, and he rose, he and him, and the two came to her.
sentences.i: He hurried back from her and went in to Tāj al-Mulūk and told him quietly what she had said; and the two of them got up together and went to her.
sentences.n: sārrahu, “he spoke to him in secret”; the bare letters (ساره) could also be read sarrahu, “he gladdened him (with this news)”, and both fit. huwa wa-iyyāhu, “he and him”, is Middle Arabic for “the two of them together”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَتْ تَاجَ الْمُلُوكِ عَانَقَتْهُ بِحَضْرَةِ أَبِيهَا وَتَعَلَّقَتْ بِهِ وَقَبَّلَتْهُ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ أَوْحَشْتَنِي
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾat tāja al-mulūki ʿānaqathu bi-ḥaḍrati abīhā wa-taʿallaqat bihi wa-qabbalathu wa-qālat lahu awḥashtanī
sentences.l: And when she saw Tāj al-Mulūk she embraced him in the presence of her father and clung to him and kissed him and said to him: You made me lonely.
sentences.i: When she saw Tāj al-Mulūk she threw her arms round him in front of her father, clung to him and kissed him, and said, “How I have missed you!”
sentences.n: The print has وفالت, a misprint for وقالت, corrected here. awḥashtanī, “you have made me desolate”, is the everyday way to say “I missed you”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ الْتَفَتَتْ إِلَى أَبِيهَا وَقَالَتْ هَلْ رَأَيْتَ أَحَدًا يُفَرِّطُ فِي مِثْلِ هٰذِهِ الذَّاتِ الْجَمِيلَةِ وَمَعَ ذٰلِكَ إِنَّهُ مَلِكٌ ابْنُ مَلِكٍ وَمِنَ الْأَحْرَارِ الْمُصَانِينَ عَنِ الرَّذَائِلِ
sentences.tr: thumma iltafatat ilā abīhā wa-qālat hal raʾayta aḥadan yufarriṭu fī mithli hādhihi al-dhāti al-jamīlati wa-maʿa dhālika innahu malikun ibnu malikin wa-mina al-aḥrāri al-muṣānīna ʿani al-radhāʾili
sentences.l: Then she turned to her father and said: Have you seen anyone (who would) squander the like of this beautiful being? And with that, he is a king son of a king, and of the free-born kept-safe from the vices.
sentences.i: Then she turned to her father and said, “Have you ever seen anyone throw away so beautiful a creature as this? And on top of that he is a king and a king's son, one of the nobly born, who are kept far from every baseness.”
sentences.n: farraṭa fī, “to let slip, to be careless with”. al-dhāt, “the person, the being”, here his whole self. al-muṣānīn, “protected, kept pure”, is formed from aṣāna where Classical would say maṣūnīn.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذٰلِكَ خَرَجَ الْمَلِكُ شَهْرَمَانُ وَرَدَّ عَلَيْهِمَا الْبَابَ بِيَدِهِ وَمَضَى إِلَى وَزِيرِ الْمَلِكِ شَاهْ سُلَيْمَانَ وَمَنْ بِصُحْبَتِهِ مِنَ الرُّسُلِ وَأَمَرَهُمْ أَنْ يُعْلِمُوا مَلِكَهُمْ أَنَّ وَلَدَهُ فِي خَيْرٍ وَسُرُورٍ وَهُوَ فِى أَلَذِّعَيْشٍ مَعَ مَعْشُوقَتِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika kharaja al-maliku shahramānu wa-radda ʿalayhimā al-bāba bi-yadihi wa-maḍā ilā wazīri al-maliki shāh sulaymāna wa-man bi-ṣuḥbatihi mina al-rusuli wa-amarahum an yuʿlimū malikahum anna waladahu fī khayrin wa-surūrin wa-huwa fī aladhdhi ʿayshin maʿa maʿshūqatihi
sentences.l: So at that King Shahramān went out and shut the door on the two of them with his hand, and went off to the vizier of King Shāh Sulaymān and those in his company of the envoys, and commanded them to let their king know that his son is in good and gladness, and he is in the most-delightful of living with his beloved.
sentences.i: At that King Shahramān went out, closing the door on the two of them with his own hand, and went to King Sulaymān Shāh's vizier and the envoys with him, and told them to let their king know that his son was well and happy, and enjoying the sweetest of lives with his beloved.
sentences.n: The print has والده (wālidahu, “his father”), a misprint for ولده (waladahu, “his son”), corrected here: it is Tāj al-Mulūk who is with his beloved. radda al-bāba ʿalā, “to close the door on”. The print runs aladhdhi ʿayshin, “the most delightful of living”, together as one word (الذّعيش), and marks its doubled dhāl; it marks the doubled dāl of radda too.

sentences.t: فَتَوَجَّهُوا إِلَى الْمَلِكِ لِيُعْلِمُوهُ بِذٰلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-tawajjahū ilā al-maliki li-yuʿlimūhu bi-dhālika
sentences.l: So they turned towards the king to let-him-know of that.
sentences.i: So they set off to the king to tell him the news.
sentences.n: The print marks the doubled jīm of tawajjahū.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْمَلِكَ شَهْرَمَانَ أَمَرَ بِإِخْرَاجِ التَّقَادُمِ وَالْعَلُوفَاتِ وَالضِّيَافَاتِ إِلَى عَسَاكِرِ الْمَلِكِ سُلَيْمَانَ شَاهْ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-malika shahramāna amara bi-ikhrāji al-taqādumi wa-al-ʿalūfāti wa-al-ḍiyāfāti ilā ʿasākiri al-maliki sulaymāna shāh
sentences.l: Then King Shahramān commanded the bringing-out of the offerings and the fodders and the hospitalities to the troops of King Sulaymān Shāh.
sentences.i: Then King Shahramān gave orders for gifts, fodder and provisions of welcome to be sent out to King Sulaymān Shāh's troops.
sentences.n: amara bi-, “to order (something)”: bi- marks what is ordered. taqādum (sing. taqdima), “presents offered to a superior”, and ʿalūfāt, “rations, fodder”, are both words of the later language.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَخْرَجُو جَمِيعَ مَا أَمَرَ بِهِ أَخْرَجَ مِائَةَ جَوَادٍ وَمِئَةَ هَجِينٍ وَمِائَةَ مَمْلُوكٍ وَمِائَةَ سُرِّيَّهٍ وَمِائَةَ عَبْدٍ وَمِائَةَ جَارِيَةٍ وَسَاقَ الْجَمِيعَ قُدَّامَهُ هَدِيَّةً
sentences.tr: fa-lammā akhrajū jamīʿa mā amara bihi akhraja miʾata jawādin wa-miʾata hajīnin wa-miʾata mamlūkin wa-miʾata surriyyatin wa-miʾata ʿabdin wa-miʾata jāriyatin wa-sāqa al-jamīʿa quddāmahu hadiyyatan
sentences.l: And when they had brought out all that he commanded, he brought out a hundred steeds and a hundred dromedaries and a hundred mamluks and a hundred concubines and a hundred black-slaves and a hundred slave-girls, and drove all-of-them before him as a gift.
sentences.i: When they had sent out everything he had ordered, he brought out a hundred thoroughbred horses, a hundred racing camels, a hundred mamluks, a hundred concubines, a hundred black slaves and a hundred slave-girls, and drove them all before him as a present.
sentences.n: akhrajū is printed without its final silent alif (اخرجو), a common habit of the print. The same word “hundred” is spelt two ways in one line, مائة and مئة; both read miʾa. surriyya, “concubine”, is printed with a final hāʾ for tāʾ marbūṭa (سريه). hajīn is a swift riding camel; ʿabd here means a black slave, beside the white mamlūk.

sentences.t: وَرَكِبَ هُوَ فِي أَكَابِرِ دَوْلَتِهِ وَخَوَاصِّهِ حَتَّى صَارُوا خَارِجَ الْمَدِينَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-rakiba huwa fī akābiri dawlatihi wa-khawāṣṣihi ḥattā ṣārū khārija al-madīnati
sentences.l: And he rode, he, among the great-ones of his state and his intimates, until they were outside the city.
sentences.i: And he himself rode out with the grandees of his realm and his closest attendants until they were outside the city.
sentences.n: rakiba fī, “to ride in (the midst of)”: at the head of a company. dawla, “state, reign”: the court and government.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا عَلِمَ السُّلْطَانُ سُلَيْمَانُ شَاهْ بِذٰلِكَ قَامَ وَتَمَشَّى خُطُوَاتٍ إِلَى لِقَائِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ʿalima al-sulṭānu sulaymānu shāh bi-dhālika qāma wa-tamashshā khuṭuwātin ilā liqāʾihi
sentences.l: And when the sultan Sulaymān Shāh knew of that, he rose and walked some steps to meeting-him.
sentences.i: When Sultan Sulaymān Shāh learned of it, he rose and walked a few steps to meet him.
sentences.n: To go a few steps to meet a guest is a mark of honour between kings.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ الْوَزِيرُ وَعَزِيزٌ أَعْلَمَاهُ بِالْخَبَرِ فَفَرِحَ وَقَالَ الْحَمْدُلِلّٰهِ الَّذِي بَلَّغَ وَلَدِي مُنَاهُ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna al-wazīru wa-ʿazīzun aʿlamāhu bi-al-khabari fa-fariḥa wa-qāla al-ḥamdu li-llāhi alladhī ballagha waladī munāhu
sentences.l: And the vizier and ʿAzīz had let-him-know the news, and he rejoiced and said: The praise (is) to God who made my son reach his desire!
sentences.i: The vizier and ʿAzīz had already told him the news, and he rejoiced and said, “Praise be to God, who has brought my son to his heart's desire!”
sentences.n: kāna … aʿlamāhu, “had informed him”: kāna with a past verb gives the pluperfect. The print runs al-ḥamdu li-llāhi together as one word (الحمدلله). ballagha … munāhu, “made reach his wish”: two objects, the person and the thing reached.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْمَلِكَ سُلَيْمَانَ شَاهْ أَخَذَ الْمَلِكَ شَهْرَمَانَ بِحِضْنِهِ وَأَجْلَسَهُ بِجَانِبِةِ عَلَى السَّرِيرِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-malika sulaymāna shāh akhadha al-malika shahramāna bi-ḥiḍnihi wa-ajlasahu bi-jānibihi ʿalā al-sarīri
sentences.l: Then King Sulaymān Shāh took King Shahramān in his bosom and seated him by his side on the throne.
sentences.i: Then King Sulaymān Shāh embraced King Shahramān and seated him beside himself on the throne.
sentences.n: bi-jānibihi, “at his side”, is printed with tāʾ marbūṭa for the pronoun -hu (بجانبة), a spelling that recurs in this passage (والدة for wāliduhu, بلادة, خاطرة).

sentences.t: وَتَحَادَثَا وَانْبَسَطَا مَعَ بَعْضِهِمَا فِى الْكَلَامِ
sentences.tr: wa-taḥādathā wa-inbasaṭā maʿa baʿḍihimā fī al-kalāmi
sentences.l: And the two talked-together and the two were at-ease with each-other in the speech.
sentences.i: And the two of them talked together and grew easy and cheerful with each other in their conversation.
sentences.n: inbasaṭa, “to be spread out, to be at ease, cheerful”. maʿa baʿḍihimā, “with each other”, is the colloquial way of saying it.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قُدِّمَ لَهُمُ الطَّعَامُ فَأَكَلُوا حَتَّى اكْتَفَوْا
sentences.tr: thumma quddima lahumu al-ṭaʿāmu fa-akalū ḥattā iktafaw
sentences.l: Then the food was brought-forward to them, and they ate until they were sufficed.
sentences.i: Then food was set before them, and they ate their fill.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قُدِّمَتْ لَهُمُ الْحَلْوِيَّاتُ فَتَحَلَّوْا وَالْفَوَاكِهُ وَالنُّقْلُ فَتَفَكَّهُوا وَتَنَقَّلُوا
sentences.tr: thumma quddimat lahumu al-ḥalwiyyātu fa-taḥallaw wa-al-fawākihu wa-al-nuqlu fa-tafakkahū wa-tanaqqalū
sentences.l: Then the sweetmeats were brought-forward to them, and they sweetened-themselves; and the fruits and the dessert, and they fruited-themselves and dessert-ed.
sentences.i: Then sweetmeats were brought them, and they ate of the sweets; and fruits and dried fruits and nuts, and they ate fruit and nibbled.
sentences.n: A play of words, each dish followed by a verb made from its own root: ḥalwiyyāt, “sweets”, taḥallaw, “they ate sweets”; fawākih, “fruits”, tafakkahū, “they ate fruit”; nuql, “dried fruit and nuts taken as dessert”, tanaqqalū, “they ate the dessert”.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَكُنْ غَيْرُ سَاعَةٍ إِلَّاوَتَاجُ الْمُلُوكِ قَدْ أَقْبَلَ عَلَيْهِمْ فِي زِيٍّ عَظِيمٍ وَزِينَةٍ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yakun ghayru sāʿatin illā wa-tāju al-mulūki qad aqbala ʿalayhim fī ziyyin ʿaẓīmin wa-zīnatin
sentences.l: And there was not other than an hour but (that) Tāj al-Mulūk had come forward upon them in a grand dress and finery.
sentences.i: It was no more than an hour before Tāj al-Mulūk came in to them, splendidly dressed and adorned.
sentences.n: lam yakun ghayru sāʿatin illā wa-…, “there was only an hour, and then …”: a narrative formula for “before long”. The print runs illā wa-tāju together as one word (الاوتاج), and marks the doubled yāʾ of ziyy, “dress, attire”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَآهُ وَالِدُةُ قَامَ إِلَيْهِ وَاحْتَضَنَهُ وَقَبَّلَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾāhu wāliduhu qāma ilayhi wa-iḥtaḍanahu wa-qabbalahu
sentences.l: And when his father saw him, he rose to him and embraced him and kissed him.
sentences.n: wāliduhu, “his father”, is printed with tāʾ marbūṭa for the pronoun (والدة). The print marks the doubled bāʾ of qabbalahu.

sentences.t: وَقَامَ جَمِيعُ مَنْ كَانَ جَالِسًا وَأَجْلَسَهُ الْمَلِكَانِ بَيْنَهُمَا وَجَلَسُوا يَتَحَدَّثُونَ سَاعَةً
sentences.tr: wa-qāma jamīʿu man kāna jālisan wa-ajlasahu al-malikāni baynahumā wa-jalasū yataḥaddathūna sāʿatan
sentences.l: And all who were sitting rose, and the two kings seated him between them, and they sat talking an hour.
sentences.i: Everyone who had been sitting rose to their feet; the two kings seated him between them, and they sat talking for a while.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ سُلَيْمَانُ شَاهْ لِلْمَلِكِ شَهْرَمَانَ إِنِّي أُرِيدُأَنْ أَكْتُبَ كِتَابَ وَلَدِي عَلَى ابْنَتِكَ عَلَى رُؤُسِ الْأَشْهَادِ لِيَشْتَهِرَ ذٰلِكَ كَمَا هُوَ السُّنَّةُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-maliku sulaymānu shāh li-al-maliki shahramāna innī urīdu an aktuba kitāba waladī ʿalā ibnatika ʿalā ruʾūsi al-ashhādi li-yashtahira dhālika kamā huwa al-sunnatu
sentences.l: Then King Sulaymān Shāh said to King Shahramān: I want to write the writ of my son upon your daughter, upon the heads of the witnesses, so that that may become-known, as is the Sunna.
sentences.i: Then King Sulaymān Shāh said to King Shahramān, “I wish to have my son's marriage contract with your daughter drawn up before witnesses, so that it is made public, as the Sunna requires.”
sentences.n: kataba kitāba X ʿalā Y, “to write X's contract upon Y”, is to draw up the marriage contract between them. ʿalā ruʾūsi al-ashhādi, “on the heads of the witnesses”: openly, before everyone. ruʾūs, “heads”, is printed with one wāw (رؤس). The print runs urīdu an together as one word (اريدان), and marks the doubled nūn of sunna, the Prophet's practice.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ السَّمْعُ وَالطَّاعَةُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-samʿu wa-al-ṭāʿatu
sentences.l: And he said to him: The hearing and the obedience.
sentences.i: And he answered him with hearing and obedience.
sentences.n: al-samʿu wa-al-ṭāʿatu, “hearing and obedience”: the formula of willing consent, here between equals as a courtesy.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذٰلِكَ أَرْسَلَ الْمَلِكُ شَهْرَمَانُ إِلَى الْقَاضِي وَالشُّهُودِ فَحَضَرُوا وَكَتَبُوا كِتَابَ تَاجِ الْمُلُوكِ عَلَى السِّتِّ دُنْيَا
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika arsala al-maliku shahramānu ilā al-qāḍī wa-al-shuhūdi fa-ḥaḍarū wa-katabū kitāba tāji al-mulūki ʿalā al-sitti dunyā
sentences.l: So at that King Shahramān sent to the judge and the witnesses, and they came and wrote the writ of Tāj al-Mulūk upon the Lady Dunyā.
sentences.i: At that King Shahramān sent for the qāḍī and the witnesses; they came and drew up the marriage contract of Tāj al-Mulūk with the Lady Dunyā.

sentences.t: وَفُرِّقَتِ الْبَقَاشِيشُ وَالسُّكَّرُ وَانْطَلَقَ الْبَخُورُ وَالطِّيبُ وَكَانَ يَوْمَ فَرَحٍ وَسُرُورٍ
sentences.tr: wa-furriqati al-baqāshīshu wa-al-sukkaru wa-inṭalaqa al-bakhūru wa-al-ṭību wa-kāna yawma faraḥin wa-surūrin
sentences.l: And the gratuities and the sugar were distributed, and the incense and the perfume were let loose, and it was a day of joy and gladness.
sentences.i: Gifts of money and sugar were handed round, incense and perfume rose on every side, and it was a day of joy and gladness.
sentences.n: baqāshīsh, plural of baqshīsh, “a gift of money, a tip”, a Persian word that came in through Turkish. Sugar and sweets were given out at weddings.

sentences.t: وَفَرِحَتْ جَمِيعُ الْأَكَابِرِ وَالْعَسَاكِرِ بِذٰلِكَ وَشَرَعَ الْمَلِكُ شَهْرَمَانُ فِي تَجْهِيزِ ابْنَتِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-fariḥat jamīʿu al-akābiri wa-al-ʿasākiri bi-dhālika wa-sharaʿa al-maliku shahramānu fī tajhīzi ibnatihi
sentences.l: And all the great-ones and the troops rejoiced at that, and King Shahramān set about the equipping of his daughter.
sentences.i: All the grandees and the soldiers rejoiced at it, and King Shahramān began preparing his daughter's trousseau.
sentences.n: tajhīz, “equipping”: here the fitting-out of a bride with her trousseau. sharaʿa fī, “to set about, begin”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ تَاجَ الْمُلُوكِ قَالَ لِوَالِدِةِ إِنَّ هٰذَا الشَّابَّ عَزِيزٌ رَجُلٌ مِنَ الْكِرَامِ وَقَدْ خَدَمَنِى خِدْمَةً عَظِيمَةً وَتَعِبَ مَعِي وَسَافَرَ مَعِي وَأَوْصَلَنِي إِلَى بُغْيَتِي وَصَبَرَ مَعِي وَيُصَبِّرُنِي حَتَّى قَضَيْتُ حَاجَتِى
sentences.tr: thumma inna tāja al-mulūki qāla li-wālidihi inna hādhā al-shābba ʿazīzun rajulun mina al-kirāmi wa-qad khadamanī khidmatan ʿaẓīmatan wa-taʿiba maʿī wa-sāfara maʿī wa-awṣalanī ilā bughyatī wa-ṣabara maʿī wa-yuṣabbirunī ḥattā qaḍaytu ḥājatī
sentences.l: Then Tāj al-Mulūk said to his father: This young-man ʿAzīz is a man of the noble-ones; and he has served me a great service, and toiled with me and travelled with me, and brought me to my desire, and was patient with me and keeps-me-patient, until I accomplished my need.
sentences.i: Then Tāj al-Mulūk said to his father, “This young man ʿAzīz is a man of true nobility. He has done me great service: he has toiled and travelled with me, brought me to my heart's desire, borne patiently with me and kept me patient, until I gained what I wanted.
sentences.n: li-wālidihi, “to his father”, printed with tāʾ marbūṭa for the pronoun (لوالدة). yuṣabbirunī, “he makes me patient, consoles me”, stands as a present among past verbs, as if to say “and kept on steadying me”. The print writes ʿAzīz without the alif that the accusative (ʿAzīzan, after inna hādhā al-shābba) would need, so it is pointed in the nominative, as the spoken language would say it.

sentences.t: وَلَهُ الْآنَ مَعِي سَنَتَانِ وَهُوَ مُشَتَّتٌ مِنْ بِلَادِهِ وَقَصْدِى أَنَّنَا نُهَيِّئُ لَهُ تِجَارَةً مِنْ هُنَا وَيُسَافِرُ مَحْبُورَ الْخَاطِرِ فَإِنَّ بِلَادِةِ قَرِيبَةٌ
sentences.tr: wa-lahu al-āna maʿī sanatāni wa-huwa mushattatun min bilādihi wa-qaṣdī annanā nuhayyiʾu lahu tijāratan min hunā wa-yusāfiru maḥbūra al-khāṭiri fa-inna bilādihi qarībatun
sentences.l: And to him now with me (are) two years, and he is scattered-away from his country; and my aim (is) that we prepare for him merchandise from here, and he travels glad of mind, for his country is near.
sentences.i: He has been with me two years now, far from his own country. My wish is that we make ready a stock of merchandise for him here, and that he set out with a glad heart, for his country is not far off.
sentences.n: lahu … sanatāni, “to him are two years”: he has spent two years. annanā nuhayyiʾu, “that we prepare”, with the present indicative after anna where Classical Arabic would say an nuhayyiʾa. maḥbūr al-khāṭir, “glad of mind” (maḥbūr, “made glad”). The second bilādihi, “his country”, is printed with tāʾ marbūṭa for the pronoun (بلادة). The print marks the doubled letters of mushattat and nuhayyiʾu.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ وَالِدُةُ نِعْمَ مَا رَأَيْتَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu wāliduhu niʿma mā raʾayta
sentences.l: And his father said to him: Excellent is what you have seen!
sentences.i: His father said to him, “That is a fine thought.”
sentences.n: niʿma mā, “excellent is what …”: niʿma is the verb of praise. raʾā, “to see”, also means “to judge, think fit”. wāliduhu is again printed والدة.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذٰلِكَ هَيَّئُوا لَهُ مِائَةَ حِمْلٍ مِنْ أَفْخَرِ الْقُمَاشِ وَأَغْلَاهُ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika hayyaʾū lahu miʾata ḥimlin min afkhari al-qumāshi wa-aghlāhu
sentences.l: So at that they prepared for him a hundred loads of the most-splendid of the stuffs and the costliest-of-it.
sentences.i: So they made ready for him a hundred loads of the finest and costliest cloth.
sentences.n: qumāsh, “cloth, fabric, goods”.

sentences.t: وَأَقْبَلَ عَلَيْهِ تَاجُ الْمُلُوكِ وَأَنْعَمَ عَلَيْهِ بِالْمَالِ الْجَزِيلِ وَوَدَّعَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-aqbala ʿalayhi tāju al-mulūki wa-anʿama ʿalayhi bi-al-māli al-jazīli wa-waddaʿahu
sentences.l: And Tāj al-Mulūk came forward to him and bestowed upon him the abundant wealth, and bade-him-farewell.
sentences.i: Tāj al-Mulūk came to him, bestowed a great sum of money on him and bade him farewell.
sentences.n: anʿama ʿalā X bi-Y, “to bestow Y on X”: bi- marks the gift. The print marks the doubled dāl of waddaʿahu.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَهُ يَا أَخِي وَصَدِيقِى خُذْ هٰذِةِ الْأَحْمَالَ وَاقْبَلْهَا مِنِّي عَلَى سَبِيلِ الْهَدِيَّةِ وَالْمَحَبَّةِ وَتَوَّجَهْ إِلَى بِلَادِكَ مَعَ السَّلَامَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lahu yā akhī wa-ṣadīqī khudh hādhihi al-aḥmāla wa-iqbalhā minnī ʿalā sabīli al-hadiyyati wa-al-maḥabbati wa-tawajjah ilā bilādika maʿa al-salāmati
sentences.l: And he said to him: O my brother and my friend, take these loads and accept them from me by way of the gift and the love, and set out to your country with the safety.
sentences.i: And he said to him, “My brother and my friend, take these loads and accept them from me as a gift and a token of love, and go home to your country in safety.”
sentences.n: hādhihi, “these”, is printed with tāʾ marbūṭa (هذة). The print sets the shadda of tawajjah, “turn, set out”, on the wāw (وتوّجه) where the word wants it on the jīm; the mark is kept, and we read the word as tawajjah. maʿa al-salāma, “with safety”, the ordinary farewell.

sentences.t: فَقَبِلَهَا مِنْهُ وَقَبَّلَ الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَبَيْنَ يَدَيْ وَالِدِةِ وَوَدَّعَهُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-qabilahā minhu wa-qabbala al-arḍa bayna yadayhi wa-bayna yaday wālidihi wa-waddaʿahum
sentences.l: So he accepted them from him, and kissed the ground between his hands and between the hands of his father, and bade-them-farewell.
sentences.i: ʿAzīz accepted them from him, kissed the ground before him and before his father, and took leave of them.
sentences.n: qabila, “to accept”, and qabbala, “to kiss”, side by side: the same letters, told apart by the doubling. bayna yadayhi, “between his hands”: in his presence. wālidihi is again printed والدة.

sentences.t: وَرَكِبَ تَاجُ الْمُلُوكِ مَعَ عَزِيزٍ حَتَّى شَيَّعَهُ قَدْرَ ثَلٰثَةِ أَمْيَالٍ وَأَخَذَ خَاطِرِةِ وَأَقْسَمَ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يَرْجِعَ بَعْدَهَا
sentences.tr: wa-rakiba tāju al-mulūki maʿa ʿazīzin ḥattā shayyaʿahu qadra thalāthati amyālin wa-akhadha khāṭirahu wa-aqsama ʿalayhi an yarjiʿa baʿdahā
sentences.l: And Tāj al-Mulūk rode with ʿAzīz until he had escorted him the measure of three miles, and took his mind, and adjured him that he return after-it.
sentences.i: Tāj al-Mulūk rode with ʿAzīz and saw him on his way for some three miles; then he bade him a kind farewell, and adjured him to turn back after that.
sentences.n: shayyaʿa, “to escort a departing guest some way”. akhadha khāṭirahu, “he took his mind”, is a colloquial idiom for comforting someone, or for taking a kindly leave. khāṭirahu is printed with tāʾ marbūṭa for the pronoun (خاطرة). The print marks the doubled yāʾ of shayyaʿahu and writes thalātha with the small alif (ثلٰثة). aqsama ʿalayhi an, “he adjured him to”. baʿdahā, “after it” (feminine), is unclear: perhaps “after that (journey)”, perhaps “after her”, his mother, whom ʿAzīz names next. It may also be that ʿAzīz is the one who begs the prince to turn back; the Arabic does not say which.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ عَزِيزٌ وَاللّٰهِ يَا سَيِّدِي لَوْلَا وَالِدَتِي مَا فَارَقْتُكَ وَلٰكِنْ يَاسَيِّدِي لَاتَقْطَعْ أَخْبَارَكَ عَنِّى
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu ʿazīzun wa-allāhi yā sayyidī lawlā wālidatī mā fāraqtuka wa-lākin yā sayyidī lā taqṭaʿ akhbāraka ʿannī
sentences.l: And ʿAzīz said to him: By God, O my master, were it not for my mother I would not have parted from you; but, O my master, do not cut off your news from me.
sentences.i: ʿAzīz said to him, “By God, my lord, were it not for my mother I would never leave you. But, my lord, do not keep me without news of you.”
sentences.n: lawlā X mā …, “were it not for X, I would not …”. The print runs yā sayyidī and lā taqṭaʿ together (ياسيدي, لاتقطع).

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ وَهُوَ كَذٰلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu wa-huwa ka-dhālika
sentences.l: And he said to him: And it is like that.
sentences.i: He answered, “So it shall be.”

sentences.t: وَرَجَعَ تَاجُ الْمُلُوكِ وَسَافَرَ عَزِيزٌ حَتَّى وَصَلَ إِلَى بِلَادِةِ
sentences.tr: wa-rajaʿa tāju al-mulūki wa-sāfara ʿazīzun ḥattā waṣala ilā bilādihi
sentences.l: And Tāj al-Mulūk returned, and ʿAzīz travelled until he arrived at his country.
sentences.i: Then Tāj al-Mulūk turned back, and ʿAzīz journeyed on until he reached his own country.
sentences.n: bilādihi is printed with tāʾ marbūṭa (بلادة).

sentences.t: فَدَخَلَ وَلَمْ يَزَلْ سَائِرًا حَتَّى دَخَلَ عَلَى أُمِّهِ فَوَجَدَهَا بَنَتْ لَهُ قَبْرًا فِي وَسْطِ الدَّارِ وَصَارَتْ تَزُورُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-dakhala wa-lam yazal sāʾiran ḥattā dakhala ʿalā ummihi fa-wajadahā banat lahu qabran fī wasṭi al-dāri wa-ṣārat tazūruhu
sentences.l: And he entered, and did not cease going until he entered upon his mother; and he found her (that) she had built for him a tomb in the middle of the house, and had taken to visiting it.
sentences.i: He entered the city and went on without stopping until he came in to his mother, and found that she had built a tomb for him in the middle of the house and had taken to visiting it.
sentences.n: dakhala ʿalā, “to go in to (a person)”. ṣārat tazūruhu, “she became visiting it”: ṣāra with a present verb means “began to, took to”. She had given him up for dead after his two years' absence.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا دَخَلَ الدَّارَ وَجَدَهَا قَدْ حَلَّتْ شَعْرَهَا وَنَشَرَتْهُ عَلَى الْقَبْرِ وَهِيَ تَبْكِي وَتَقُولُ شِعْرٌ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā dakhala al-dāra wajadahā qad ḥallat shaʿrahā wa-nasharathu ʿalā al-qabri wa-hiya tabkī wa-taqūlu shiʿrun
sentences.l: And when he entered the house, he found her (that) she had loosed her hair and spread it over the tomb, and she was weeping and saying — poetry:
sentences.i: When he entered the house he found she had unbound her hair and spread it over the tomb, and she was weeping and saying:
sentences.n: Loosening the hair is a gesture of mourning. shaʿr, “hair”, and shiʿr, “poetry”, are the same letters, a few words apart. The print marks the doubled lām of ḥallat.

sentences.t:
وَاِنِّيْ لَصَبَّارٌ عَلَى كُلِّ حَادِثٍ * وَلٰكِنَّنِي مِنْ خُطَّةِ الْبَيْنِ اَجْزَعُ
وَمَنْ ذَا يُطِيقُ الصَّبْرَ بَعْدَ خَلِيلِهِ * وَمَنْ ذَا لِوَشْكِ الْبَيْنِ لَا يَتَضَعْضَعُ
sentences.tr:
wa-innī la-ṣabbārun ʿalā kulli ḥādithin * wa-lākinnanī min khuṭṭati al-bayni ajzaʿu
wa-man dhā yuṭīqu al-ṣabra baʿda khalīlihi * wa-man dhā li-washki al-bayni lā yataḍaʿḍaʿu
sentences.l:
And I indeed am a great-endurer upon every happening, * but I, from the matter of the parting, am-in-anguish.
And who (is) this (that) can-bear the patience after his close-friend, * and who (is) this (that) at the nearness of the parting is not shaken?
sentences.i:
I can bear with patience every blow that falls, * but at the thought of parting I lose heart.
Who can keep patience once their dearest friend is gone, * and who, when parting is at hand, does not break down?
sentences.n: la-ṣabbārun: la- adds emphasis after inna, and ṣabbār is the intensive form, “very patient”. khuṭṭa, “plan, matter, affair”. man dhā, “who is it that …?”. washk, “nearness, imminence”. yataḍaʿḍaʿu, “to be humbled, to collapse”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ صَعَّدَتِ الزَّفَرَاتِ وَأَنْشَدَتْ هٰذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: thumma ṣaʿʿadati al-zafarāti wa-anshadat hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: Then she sent-up the sighs and recited these verses:
sentences.i: Then she heaved deep sighs and recited these lines:
sentences.n: ṣaʿʿada al-zafarāt, “to send up sighs”: form II of ṣaʿida, “to rise”, made transitive. The speaker is ʿAzīz's mother, weeping at the tomb she has built for him.

sentences.t:
مَالِي مَرَرْتُ عَلَى الْقُبُوْرِ مُسَلِّما * قَبْرِ الْحَبِيْبِ فَلَمْ يَرُدَّ جَوَابِي
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ وَكَيْفَ رَدُّ جَوَابِكُمْ * وَاَنَا رَهِينُ جَنَادِلٍ وَتُرَابِي
اَكَلَ التُّرَابُ مَحَاسِنِي فَنَسِيتُكُمْ * وَحُجِبْتُ عَنْ اَهْلِي وَعَنْ اَحْبَابِي
sentences.tr:
mā lī marartu ʿalā al-qubūri musalliman * qabri al-ḥabībi fa-lam yarudda jawābī
qāla al-ḥabību wa-kayfa raddu jawābikum * wa-anā rahīnu janādilin wa-turābī
akala al-turābu maḥāsinī fa-nasītukum * wa-ḥujibtu ʿan ahlī wa-ʿan aḥbābī
sentences.l:
What is (it) with me? I passed by the graves greeting — the grave of the beloved — and he did not return my answer.
The beloved said: And how (can there be) the return of your answer, when I am pledge of rocks and dust?
The dust has eaten my beauties, so I have forgotten you, and I have been veiled from my people and from my loved-ones.
sentences.i:
Why is it that I passed by the graves with a greeting, by my beloved's grave, and he gave me no answer back?
The beloved said: How should I answer you, when I lie in pledge to stones and dust?
The dust has eaten up my beauty, and I have forgotten you; I am shut away from my family and from those I loved.
sentences.n: The first line is the mourner's; the second and third are the dead one's reply. qabri al-ḥabībi is in the genitive because it picks up al-qubūri, “the graves”: “by the graves — by the beloved's grave”. rahīn, “held in pledge”: the dead man is held by the stones and earth of the grave as a pawn is held. turābī ends in -ī for the rhyme, as the other lines do, though it reads as plain “dust” here, not “my dust”.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا هِيَ كَذٰلِكَ وَإِذَا بِعَزِيزٍ أَقْبَلَ وَدَخَلَ عَلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā hiya ka-dhālika wa-idhā bi-ʿazīzin aqbala wa-dakhala ʿalayhā
sentences.l: And while she (was) thus, and behold, ʿAzīz came-forward and entered upon her.
sentences.i: And while she was so, all at once there was ʿAzīz, coming up and walking in on her.
sentences.n: wa-idhā bi-, “and behold”: the bi- only marks who appears. dakhala ʿalā, “to go in to someone”, to enter where they are.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَتْهُ وَقَعَتْ مَغْشِيًّا عَلَيْهَا مِنَ الْفَرَحِ فَنَضَحَ عَلَى وَجْهِهَا الْمَاءَ فَأَفَاقَتْ وَقَامَتْ وَأَخَذَتْهُ فِي حِضْنِهَا وَضَمَّتْهُ وَضَمَّهَا وَسَلَّمَ عَلَيْهَا وَسَلَّمَتْ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾathu waqaʿat maghshiyyan ʿalayhā mina al-faraḥi fa-naḍaḥa ʿalā wajhihā al-māʾa fa-afāqat wa-qāmat wa-akhadhathu fī ḥiḍnihā wa-ḍammathu wa-ḍammahā wa-sallama ʿalayhā wa-sallamat ʿalayhi
sentences.l: And when she saw him, she fell fainted-upon from the joy; so he sprinkled on her face the water, and she came-to and rose, and took him into her bosom, and she pressed him and he pressed her, and he greeted her and she greeted him.
sentences.i: When she saw him she fell down in a faint for joy. He sprinkled water on her face and she came round and stood up, and took him in her arms; she held him close and he held her, and they greeted one another.
sentences.n: maghshiyyan ʿalayhā, “fainted”, literally “covered over (by a swoon)”: the stock phrase keeps the masculine maghshiyyan even of a woman, with ʿalayhā carrying the gender. The print marks the doubled mīm of ḍammathu and ḍammahā.

sentences.t: وَسَأَلَتْهُ عَنْ سَبَبِ غِيَابِهِ فَحَكَى لَهَا عَلَى مَا وَقَعَ لَهُ مِنَ الْأَوَّلِ إِلَى الْآخِرِ
sentences.tr: wa-saʾalathu ʿan sababi ghiyābihi fa-ḥakā lahā ʿalā mā waqaʿa lahu mina al-awwali ilā al-ākhiri
sentences.l: And she asked him about the cause of his absence, so he told her of what befell him from the first to the last.
sentences.i: She asked him why he had been away so long, and he told her everything that had happened to him, from beginning to end.
sentences.n: ḥakā ʿalā mā, “told about what”: Classical ḥakā takes its object directly, and the ʿalā is a habit of the spoken language. The print writes saʾalathu and al-ākhir with their hamza and madda.

sentences.t: وَأَخْبَرَهَا أَنَّ تَاجَ الْمُلُوكِ أَعْطَاهُ مِنَ الْمَالِ وَالْأَقْمِشَةِ مِائَةَ حِمْلٍ فَفَرِحَتْ بِذٰلِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-akhbarahā anna tāja al-mulūki aʿṭāhu mina al-māli wa-al-aqmishati miʾata ḥimlin fa-fariḥat bi-dhālika
sentences.l: And he informed her that Tāj al-Mulūk gave him of the wealth and the stuffs a hundred loads, and she rejoiced at that.
sentences.i: And he told her that Tāj al-Mulūk had given him a hundred loads of money and fine cloth, and she was glad of it.
sentences.n: ḥiml, “a load”, as much as one beast carries. aqmisha, “fabrics”, plural of qumāsh.

sentences.t: وَأَقَامَ عَزِيزٌ عِنْدَ وَالِدَتِهِ فِي بَلْدَتِهِ يَبْكِي عَلَى مَا وَقَعَ لَهُ مِنْ بِنْتِ الدَّلِيلَةِ الْمُحْتَالَةِ الَّتِي خَصَتْهُ
sentences.tr: wa-aqāma ʿazīzun ʿinda wālidatihi fī baldatihi yabkī ʿalā mā waqaʿa lahu min binti al-dalīlati al-muḥtālati allatī khaṣathu
sentences.l: And ʿAzīz stayed with his mother in his town, weeping over what befell him from the daughter of the Dalīla the wily, who castrated him.
sentences.i: And ʿAzīz stayed on with his mother in his own town, weeping over what had been done to him by the daughter of Dalīla the wily, who had castrated him.
sentences.n: bint al-dalīla: the print puts the article on the name Dalīla, which normally has none. khaṣathu, from khaṣā, “to castrate”; this is the mutilation ʿAzīz suffered earlier in his story.

sentences.t: هٰذَا مَا وَقَعَ لِعَزِيزٍ
sentences.tr: hādhā mā waqaʿa li-ʿazīzin
sentences.l: This (is) what befell ʿAzīz.
sentences.i: So much for what happened to ʿAzīz.
sentences.n: A storyteller's formula for closing off one thread before taking up another, answered by wa-ammā mā kāna min amri … in the next sentence.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ تَاجِ الْمُلُوكِ فَإِنَّهُ دَخَلَ بِمَحْبُوبَتِهِ السِّتِّ دُنْيَا وَأَزَالَ بَكَارَتَهَا
sentences.tr: wa-ammā mā kāna min amri tāji al-mulūki fa-innahu dakhala bi-maḥbūbatihi al-sitti dunyā wa-azāla bakāratahā
sentences.l: And as for what was of the affair of Tāj al-Mulūk, he went-in with his beloved, the Lady Dunyā, and removed her virginity.
sentences.i: As for Tāj al-Mulūk, he consummated his marriage with his beloved, the Lady Dunyā, and took her virginity.
sentences.n: dakhala bi-, “to go in with (a bride)”: the regular expression for consummating a marriage.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْمَلِكَ شَهْرَمَانَ شَرَعَ فِي تَجْهِيزِ ابْنَتِهِ لِلسَّفَرِ مَعَ زَوْجِهَا وَأَبِيهَا فَأَحْضَرَ لَهُمُ الزَّادَ وَالْهَدَايَا وَالتُّحَفَ فَحَمَلُوا وَسَارُوا
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-malika shahramāna sharaʿa fī tajhīzi ibnatihi li-al-safari maʿa zawjihā wa-abīhā fa-aḥḍara lahumu al-zāda wa-al-hadāyā wa-al-tuḥafa fa-ḥamalū wa-sārū
sentences.l: Then King Shahramān began in fitting-out his daughter for the journey with her husband and her father; and he brought for them the provisions and the gifts and the rarities, and they loaded and set-out.
sentences.i: Then King Shahramān set about making his daughter ready to travel with her husband and her father. He had provisions, gifts and precious things brought for them, and they loaded up and set off.
sentences.n: wa-abīhā, “and her father”: Shahramān himself, who rides with them for the first three days; abīhi, “his father”, Sulaymān Shāh, may be meant. sharaʿa fī, “to set about, begin”.

sentences.t: وَسَارَ مَعَهُمُ الْمَلِكُ شَهْرَمَانُ ثَلٰثَةَ أَيَّامٍ لِأَجْلِ الْوَدَاعِ فَأَقْسَمَ عَلَيْهِ الْمَلِكُ شَاهْ سُلَيْمَانُ بِالرُّجُوعِ فَرَجَعَ
sentences.tr: wa-sāra maʿahumu al-maliku shahramānu thalāthata ayyāmin li-ajli al-wadāʿi fa-aqsama ʿalayhi al-maliku shāh sulaymānu bi-al-rujūʿi fa-rajaʿa
sentences.l: And King Shahramān went with them three days for the sake of the farewell; then King Shāh Sulaymān adjured him by the returning, and he returned.
sentences.i: King Shahramān rode with them for three days to see them on their way, until King Sulaymān Shāh begged him on his oath to turn back, and he went home.
sentences.n: aqsama ʿalayhi bi-, “to adjure someone to do something”, to put him on his oath. The king's name is printed here in the order Shāh Sulaymān. The print spells thalātha without its long alif (ثلٰثة) and marks it with the small alif itself.

sentences.t: وَمَازَالَ تَاجُ الْمُلُوكِ وَوَالِدُهُ وَزَوْجَتُهُ وَعَسَاكِرُهُمْ سَائِرِينَ فِى اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ حَتَّى أَشْرَفُوا عَلَى مَدِينَتِهِمْ
sentences.tr: wa-mā zāla tāju al-mulūki wa-wāliduhu wa-zawjatuhu wa-ʿasākiruhum sāʾirīna fī al-layli wa-al-nahāri ḥattā ashrafū ʿalā madīnatihim
sentences.l: And Tāj al-Mulūk and his father and his wife and their troops did not cease journeying in the night and the day until they looked-down upon their city.
sentences.i: And Tāj al-Mulūk, his father, his wife and their armies travelled on night and day until their city came in sight below them.
sentences.n: The print runs mā zāla together (ومازال). ashrafa ʿalā, “to overlook, come within sight of”, from a height.

sentences.t: فَتَوَاتَرَتِ الْأَخْبَارُ بِقُدُومِهِمْ فَزُيِّنَتْ لَهُمُ الْمَدِينَةُ
sentences.tr: fa-tawātarati al-akhbāru bi-qudūmihim fa-zuyyinat lahumu al-madīnatu
sentences.l: And the tidings followed-one-another of their arrival, and the city was adorned for them.
sentences.i: News of their coming went round, one report on the heels of another, and the city was decked out for them.
sentences.n: tawātara, “to follow in close succession”. zuyyinat, passive of form II zayyana, “to decorate”; the print marks the doubled yāʾ.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَ زَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahra zāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: And morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
sentences.n: The print sets the name as two words here, شهر زاد.
